# Project brief: <your product's name>

Write this in Module 1 (*Problem and audience*). Keep it to one page. Replace every line in angle brackets.

## User and decision

- Who uses the product: <one kind of person, for example "help-desk staff of a small shop">
- The decision or task it helps with: <one sentence, for example "answer a customer's policy question correctly">
- How they do it today, and what goes wrong: <one or two sentences, with a real example>

## Documents

- Which documents the product reads: <a narrow collection: what, how many, in which formats>
- Who owns them, and why you may use them: <permission, licence, or "synthetic, written for this project">

## What success looks like

- <one observable result, for example "staff get a cited answer, or a clear 'the documents do not say', in under 5 seconds">

## Non-goals

What the product will NOT do. Each line protects your time.

- <for example "no chat history", "no answers to customers directly", "no agent that takes actions">

## Track

- [ ] Standard track: the supplied two-shop data pack
- [ ] Own-idea track: my own domain and documents (permissioned or synthetic)

## Milestones

| Milestone | Done when | Week |
|---|---|---|
| Design pack | the architecture and the threat and cost review are written | <1> |
| One journey | a new user uploads a document and gets a cited answer | <2> |
| Safe and reliable | the wrong-shop, missing-source, invalid-file and timeout cases pass | <3> |
| Evaluated | the held-out report is written | <4> |
| Shipped | a clean computer runs the demo from the README | <5> |
